working_title: She Grew Up in Front of Us
thesis: Hayden Panettiere spent almost her entire life being watched. She entered the business before she could form memories, became famous while still growing up, and spent adulthood increasingly speaking in her own voice about the person behind the public image.
contradiction: The public knew her face for decades, but much of her later life was about defining herself beyond the roles, expectations and scrutiny that arrived before adulthood.
emotional_question: What happens when the world forms an idea of you before you have had the chance to form one of yourself?
final_thought: Her death is the trigger for attention, but the story is the life that came before it — and the fact that, near the end, she was increasingly narrating that life in her own words.

narrative_arc.name: Before Memory
narrative_arc.purpose: Establish that the camera arrived before conscious choice.

narrative_arc.name: The World Learns Her Name
narrative_arc.purpose: Show the transition from working child actor to globally recognizable performer.

narrative_arc.name: The Cost of Visibility
narrative_arc.purpose: Address publicly documented struggles without reducing her identity to them.

narrative_arc.name: Grief and Return
narrative_arc.purpose: Show loss, continued work and return to a major franchise.

narrative_arc.name: Taking the Story Back
narrative_arc.purpose: Center the memoir and her willingness to speak more explicitly about identity, privacy and her own life.

narrative_arc.name: The Final Chapter
narrative_arc.purpose: State only verified death facts and preserve uncertainty where official findings remain pending.

visual_motif: Cameras and flashes contrasted with increasingly quiet, private-feeling frames: early publicity, stages, press lines, then books, empty dressing rooms, still portraits and negative space.
visual_language: no AI likeness presented as documentary evidence
prohibited_angles: reducing the story to relationships or scandal

format_adaptations.carousel: 9-slide life arc with death withheld until final two slides
format_adaptations.single_image: deep-caption portrait led by the thesis
format_adaptations.short_form: contradiction-first: famous before identity had fully formed
format_adaptations.long_form: 12-15 minute documentary essay centered on lifelong visibility and authorship of self

script_rules: Every factual narration sentence must map to at least one approved Claim ID.
Interpretive narration must be traceable to approved interpretive claims.
Unknowns remain unknown; do not write around them.
Death occupies roughly final 10-15 percent unless new verified facts materially change editorial significance.
Use copyrighted film/TV clips only when the clip directly illustrates commentary or criticism and is tracked in the Clip Ledger.
